title: Health and the body: me duele la cabeza
summary: Name the parts of the body, say what hurts with doler, describe symptoms with estar and tener, and understand the doctor.
focus: Talking about pain, symptoms and a visit to the doctor
content:
## Twelve parts of the body

These are the parts of the body you will need most. Learn each noun with its article: the gender matters when you describe pain.

| Spanish | English | Spanish | English |
|---|---|---|---|
| la cabeza | head | la espalda | back |
| la garganta | throat | el brazo | arm |
| el estómago | stomach | la mano | hand |
| la muela | back tooth, molar | la pierna | leg |
| el ojo | eye | la rodilla | knee |
| el oído | ear (inner ear) | el pie | foot |

Two traps: **la mano** is feminine although it ends in **-o**, and **el pie** keeps a plain **-s** in the plural: **los pies**.

## Me duele, me duelen

**Doler** (to hurt) works exactly like **gustar**. The part that hurts is the subject, so the verb agrees with it. The person in pain is an indirect object pronoun (**me, te, le, nos, os, les**):

| | one part | several parts |
|---|---|---|
| I | **me duele** la cabeza | **me duelen** los pies |
| you | **te duele** la espalda | **te duelen** las muelas |
| he / she / usted | **le duele** el estómago | **le duelen** las piernas |

Use the article, never the possessive: *me duele **la** cabeza*, not *mi cabeza*. To make the person clear, add **a** + name: *A Marta le duele la espalda.*

The six forms are **duelo, dueles, duele, dolemos, doléis, duelen**. They show the stem change from **o** to **ue**, but in real life you will only hear **duele** and **duelen**.

## Estar and tener for how you feel

Spanish uses two verbs for symptoms.

**Estar** + adjective for a state (it agrees in gender and number):

- *Estoy enfermo / enferma.* I am ill.
- *Estoy resfriada.* I have a cold.
- *Estamos cansados.* We are tired.
- *Está mareado.* He is dizzy.

**Tener** + noun for a symptom you "have":

- *Tengo fiebre.* I have a fever.
- *Tengo tos.* I have a cough.
- *Tengo dolor de cabeza / de muelas / de estómago.* I have a headache / toothache / stomach ache.

**Tengo dolor de cabeza** and **me duele la cabeza** mean the same. The second is more common in conversation. To say you feel bad in general: **Me encuentro mal** or **Estoy fatal**.

## At the doctor's

The doctor speaks to you as **usted**, so the pronoun is **le**:

- *¿Qué le pasa?* What is the matter with you? (a friend asks *¿Qué te pasa?*)
- *¿Desde cuándo?* Since when?
- *¿Le duele aquí?* Does it hurt here?

Instructions come as **usted** commands (the forms you met in the imperative lesson):

- *Tome una pastilla cada ocho horas.* Take one tablet every eight hours.
- *Descanse dos días.* Rest for two days.
- *Beba mucha agua.* Drink plenty of water.
- *Abra la boca.* Open your mouth.

Getting better is **ponerse bien**: *Si descansas, te pones bien pronto.* To wish it on someone: **¡Que te mejores!** (get well soon).

vocabulary.example: Le duele el estómago después de comer.
A mi padre le duele la espalda.
Me duelen las piernas de tanto andar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My legs ache from so much walking.

vocabulary.example: Después de correr me duelen los pies.
Tengo dolor de muelas y voy al dentista.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I have a toothache and I'm going to the dentist.

vocabulary.example: Tengo fiebre: treinta y ocho y medio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I have a fever: thirty-eight and a half.
I've had a cough since Monday.

vocabulary.example: Estoy resfriada y no puedo ir a trabajar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I have a cold and I can't go to work.

vocabulary.example: Mi hijo está enfermo y tiene fiebre.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My son is ill and has a fever.

vocabulary.example: Tome una pastilla cada ocho horas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Take one pill every eight hours.

vocabulary.example: Si descansas, te pones bien pronto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you rest, you'll get better soon.

quiz.explanation: The subject is 'la cabeza', one thing, so the verb is singular: 'Me duele la cabeza.' 'Duelo' would mean 'I hurt (someone)', which is not what you mean.
hints: How many things hurt: one or several?

quiz.prompt: Complete with the right pronoun: A mi padre ___ duele la espalda.
quiz.explanation: 'A mi padre' is a third person, so the indirect object pronoun is 'le': 'A mi padre le duele la espalda.'
hints: The same pronoun you use with gustar for él/ella.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the right form of doler: Después de correr me ___ las piernas y los pies.
quiz.explanation: 'Las piernas y los pies' is plural, so the verb is plural: 'me duelen'.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence means 'I have a cold and a cough'?
quiz.explanation: 'Resfriado/a' is a temporary state, so it takes estar; 'tos' is a symptom you have, so it takes tener.
hints: A cold is a temporary state.
Symptoms that are nouns go with tener.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the right form of tener: (yo) ___ fiebre y me duele el estómago.
quiz.explanation: Fever is a symptom you 'have': 'Tengo fiebre.' The stomach ache uses doler with 'me'.
hints: The same verb as for being cold or hungry.

quiz.prompt: Hoy no voy a trabajar: ___ enfermo y me duele la garganta.
quiz.explanation: Being ill is a temporary state, so 'estoy enfermo'. 'Soy enfermo' would describe a permanent condition and 'tengo enfermo' does not exist in Spanish.
hints: A state that will pass takes estar.
Enfermo is an adjective, not a noun.

quiz.prompt: The doctor says to you (usted): '___ una pastilla cada ocho horas.'
quiz.explanation: Doctors address patients as usted, and the usted command of tomar is 'tome'. 'Toma' is the tú command and 'tomas' means 'you take'.
hints: Formal 'you' commands use the subjunctive form.
For -ar verbs, the usted command ends in -e.

quiz.prompt: Complete with a part of the body: Tengo dolor de ___ y voy al dentista.
quiz.explanation: Toothache is 'dolor de muelas', with the plural and no article; 'la muela' is a back tooth.
hints: Who do you see about this pain?
Spanish usually says it in the plural.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the right form of ponerse: Descansa y bebe agua: así te ___ bien pronto.
quiz.explanation: 'Ponerse bien' means to get better; with 'te' the tú form is 'te pones bien'. The future 'te pondrás bien' is also correct.

listening.note: The article, not the possessive: la garganta.

listening.text: Tengo fiebre desde ayer por la noche.
listening.meaning: I've had a fever since last night.
listening.note: A symptom you have takes tener.

listening.text: A Carlos le duele mucho el estómago.
Estoy resfriado y me duele la cabeza.
listening.meaning: I have a cold and my head hurts.

listening.text: Después del partido me duele mucho la espalda.
listening.meaning: After the match my back hurts a lot.
listening.note: New word: el partido = the match.

listening.text: Mi hija tiene tos y hoy no va al colegio.
listening.meaning: My daughter has a cough and isn't going to school today.
listening.note: New word: el colegio = the school.

listening.text: Tome estas pastillas tres veces al día y se pondrá bien pronto.
listening.meaning: Take these pills three times a day and you'll get better soon.

guide.tip: Think of doler as 'to be painful to'. The body part is the subject and the sufferer is me/te/le. That is why it is 'me duele LA cabeza', never 'mi cabeza'.

conversations.title: At the doctor's
conversations.scenario: Elena has felt terrible since the weekend and goes to see Doctor Ruiz at the health centre.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Buenos días. Siéntese, por favor. ¿Qué le pasa?
lines.meaning: Good morning. Sit down, please. What is the matter?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Buenos días, doctor. Me encuentro fatal. Me duele la cabeza y tengo mucha tos.
lines.meaning: Good morning, doctor. I feel awful. My head hurts and I have a bad cough.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Desde el sábado. Y creo que tengo fiebre.
lines.meaning: Since Saturday. And I think I have a fever.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: A ver… Treinta y ocho y medio. ¿Le duele la garganta?
lines.meaning: Let's see… Thirty-eight and a half. Does your throat hurt?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, mucho. Y me duele todo el cuerpo.
lines.meaning: Yes, a lot. And my whole body aches.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Abra la boca, por favor… Bueno, no es nada grave. Está resfriada y tiene un poco de fiebre.
lines.meaning: Open your mouth, please… Well, it is nothing serious. You have a cold and a slight fever.
lines.note: usted command abra; estar resfriada; tener fiebre

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Can I go to work tomorrow?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: No. Descanse dos o tres días, tome una pastilla cada ocho horas y beba mucha agua.
lines.meaning: No. Rest for two or three days, take one tablet every eight hours and drink plenty of water.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Este jarabe, dos cucharadas por la noche. Si no se pone bien en una semana, vuelva.
lines.meaning: This syrup, two spoonfuls at night. If you are not better in a week, come back.
lines.note: ponerse bien; vuelva is the usted command of volver

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Thank you very much, doctor. Goodbye.

bites.title: Doler works like gustar
bites.rule: The thing that hurts is the subject, so the verb is duele (one thing) or duelen (several). The person in pain is me, te, le, nos, os or les.
bites.example: Me duele la cabeza. Me duelen los pies.
bites.example_meaning: My head hurts. My feet hurt.

bites.title: The article, not 'my'
bites.rule: Spanish says 'the head hurts me', not 'my head hurts': me duele la cabeza, never mi cabeza. Add 'a' + name to say who: a Juan le duele.
bites.example: A Marta le duele la espalda.

bites.title: Estar for states, tener for symptoms
bites.rule: Use estar with adjectives for a state: estoy enfermo, resfriado, cansado, mareado. Use tener with nouns for a symptom: tengo fiebre, tos, dolor de muelas.
bites.example_meaning: I have a cold and a fever.

bites.title: At the doctor's
bites.rule: The doctor uses usted: ¿Qué le pasa? Then the orders come as usted commands: tome, descanse, beba, abra. Getting better is ponerse bien.

sorts.title: Duele or duelen?
sorts.why: The body part is the subject: one part takes duele, several parts take duelen.

sorts.title: Estar or tener?
sorts.why: Adjectives describing a state go with estar. Nouns naming a symptom go with tener.

sorts.title: Who is in pain?
sorts.why: Yo takes me, tú takes te, and él / ella / usted takes le, as with gustar.

spots.why: 'La cabeza' is singular, so the verb is duele.
With doler, Spanish uses the article, not the possessive: me duele la garganta.

spots.sentence: Tengo muy resfriado y no puedo salir.
spots.why: Resfriado is an adjective describing a state: estoy resfriado.
Fiebre is a noun, a symptom you have: tengo fiebre.

spots.sentence: Doctor, me duelo mucho la espalda.
spots.why: The back is the subject, so the verb is third person: me duele la espalda.

spots.sentence: Señora, toma una pastilla cada ocho horas.
spots.why: 'Señora' is addressed as usted, so the command is tome.

builds.meaning: I have a cold and a cough.
